# Parity dashboard

One row per manifest bucket in `tests/visual/data/*.json` (28, alphabetical — D7, plans/parity-dashboard-refresh/decisions.md). **engine** names the plugin that owns the bucket, or the still-unbuilt Phase D mission that will; **corpus** is the bucket's fixture count; **oracle** is how many of those fixtures have a cached PlantUML jar SVG under `test-results/dot-cache/<type>/`; **DOT equal** reads `tests/oracle/svg-conformance/dot-parity.json` (structure: cluster nesting, wrapper chain, title table, edges); **layoutEqual** is `equal/comparable` read from the same survey file as **survey** (the geometry of our layout graph against the jar's svek DOT, `tests/oracle/layout-parity.ts`; fixtures with no comparison are not counted); **ratchet pins**, **diff-baseline**, **routing** and **refusal** read the committed goldens under `oracle/goldens/`. Every empty cell names why it is empty, per the vocabulary in decisions.md D8 — a bare `n/a` never appears. `n/a (plantuml-engine only)` marks a type whose every cached jar SVG is PlantUML's own "Diagram not supported by this release" page: the port draws it, the pinned jar declines it, so nothing can be compared until a jar that supports the type is pinned. A bucket with no engine keeps its real **oracle** count but repeats its `no engine (Dn todo)` reason in every comparison cell: this port answers such a source with the dispatcher's error sentinel, so a routing or refusal count there would measure nothing. The `unknown` row is the one exception: it keeps its `n/a (accounting bucket)` engine cell — it is not a todo, D8 of `plans/unknown-bucket-routing-repair/decisions.md` — but every other column reports every measurement its oracle allows.

**corpus** counts manifest rows, which `scripts/classify-corpus.ts` guessed by keyword; **oracle** counts cached rows under `test-results/dot-cache/<type>/`, placed by the jar's own `data-diagram-type` (oracle-gap-capture D2, #109), so the two columns differ: a manifest row's oracle can live in another bucket, and a bucket can hold oracles no manifest row of that name asked for.

**survey** and **census** differ by RENDER PATH, not measurer. Both already measure text through the same system — `WidthTableMeasurer`, re-exported as `DeterministicMeasurer` (`src/core/measurer-deterministic.ts`) — over the SAME cached corpus. Survey renders every bucket through production `renderSync`. The ratchet and census helpers (`tests/oracle/svg-conformance/render-fixture-*.ts`) split: class, component, usecase, unknown, dot, gantt, mindmap, salt, wbs and files also call `renderSync`; object, state, sequence, activity, json, yaml and hcl drive their engine's own parse → layout → render pipeline with the measurer injected. A `diverged` survey verdict beside a passing byte-exact ratchet is that path difference, never a text-metric mismatch. The class ratchet and census also cover the 287 `unknown` fixtures the port routes to the class engine (`test-results/dot-cache/unknown/`, `routing-baseline.json` `ourType: CLASS`), which is why both exceed class's **oracle** count.

### Why a row falls short

**†** **Laid out by a different Graphviz.** PlantUML lays these diagrams out with Smetana, its Java translation of Graphviz 2.38. We use dot-engine, which follows current Graphviz. Elements, labels, colours and structure match, but edge routing and node spacing can differ, so most fixtures end as structural matches. This is a settled decision, not a to-do: see [Why no Smetana support?](../docs-site/guide/why-no-smetana.md). Applies to hcl, json, yaml.

**‡** **No engine yet.** We do not draw this diagram type yet, so these fixtures get an error page.

- **ditaa:** Dropped on purpose: its library is LGPL-3.0 and the MIT edition disables it (`DIVERGENCES.md`).
- **network:** This bucket is filled by a keyword match and holds no nwdiag diagrams: one description diagram, which conforms, and two in the legacy `(*) -->` activity syntax, drawn by the legacy activity engine (#123) and pinned in `svg-activity-legacy`. The 68 real nwdiag fixtures are counted under `unknown`: the nwdiag engine (#124) draws all 68 conformant (4 are jar error pages where we also error), pinned in `svg-nwdiag`.

**§** **Open defects.** An engine exists, and what remains are bugs still to fix. No library forces them.

- **activity:** Not a regression: the 5 rows short of conformant are named. Three are LaTeX under KaTeX and one is a QR code under the MIT edition (DIVERGENCES.md); `rekefe-90` prints `%version()` and waits on #155. The legacy `(*) -->` syntax is drawn by the legacy activity engine (#123), pinned in `svg-activity-legacy`.
- **class:** Not a regression: all 43 rows short of conformant are fixtures #109 captured on 2026-11-04. The layout matches on most of them (layoutEqual 641 of 664); the first differences are element ids, strokes, font sizes and fills, not yet diagnosed row by row.
- **dot:** The two structural matches are fixtures #109 captured on 2026-11-04; their geometry is not yet diagnosed.
- **sequence:** Not a regression: all 9 rows short of conformant are fixtures #109 captured on 2026-11-04. One draws our error page where PlantUML draws a diagram (`partition` as a grouping keyword, which we do not parse); the rest differ in a title child count, a dash pattern and path data.
- **state:** state-divergence-drive (#112, 2026-11-04) took the 174 open rows to 2, and the border-point anchor fix (graphviz issue 39, reclassified as ours) closed `viroxo-69-fito663`: 298 of 299 conformant. `xetase-70-zaza808` is a `{{ }}` edge label the flat creole seam cannot embed (#144, chained on #136).

**¶** **Mixed bucket.** This bucket holds sources the classifier could not assign, so its causes differ.

- **unknown:** Of the 76 fixtures short of conformant, by PlantUML's own type: 14 are types we draw imperfectly (description 5, git 4, class 2, hcl 2, help 1); 56 carry no type tag (creole, math, LaTeX and error pages); 6 are pages PlantUML itself declines.

**‖** **Nothing to compare against.** The pinned PlantUML jar answers "Diagram not supported by this release" while we draw the diagram. Applies to chronology.

- **c4:** Drawn by the description engine, with two class rows and one ELK row: 10 of 11 conformant since c4-divergence-drive (#114), 9 pinned. The last, `gikaju-64`, is a jar error page where we draw, a signed entry in `oracle/accepted-divergences.json`.

A suffix such as `(3 error)` is not a shortfall. PlantUML draws an error page for those fixtures too, and we draw our own, which counts as conformant.

## Legend

- **comparable** — fixtures classified to this type (cached canonical SVG `data-diagram-type`) whose PlantUML svek DOT was diffable against ours. Excludes **oracle-blind**.
- **equal** — of the comparable fixtures, how many are structurally EQUAL per every check in `tests/oracle/svek-dot.ts`.
- **oracle-blind** — `!pragma layout elk` fixtures (smetana/vizjs are graphviz under other names and are captured normally, per DIVERGENCES.md); PlantUML only dumps svek DOT on the graphviz path, so there is no oracle DOT to diff for elk. Excluded from **comparable**.
- **n/a (no DOT stage)** — sequence, activity, json, yaml, hcl, dot, gitgraph, board, chart, chronology, files, packet, ditaa, ebnf, gantt, mindmap, network, regex, salt, timing, wbs and wire never emit PlantUML's svek DOT upstream (DIVERGENCES.md; CLAUDE.md "One layout engine"; every one after gitgraph is a `TitledDiagram`/`DirectOsDiagram` or, for chronology, has no factory in this source tree), so they cannot have a DOT-parity row regardless of how much oracle data is cached.
- **no oracle captured** — no cached oracle DOT dump under `test-results/dot-cache/<type>/` yet, or the type has no fixture manifest; not a failure, just unmeasured.
- **no data-diagram-type classification** — oracle DOT is cached but no canonical SVG carries this type's expected `data-diagram-type` tag; run with `--type-tag` to classify.
